chapter: Washington clubs, Louis Jordan and Sarah Vaughan, 1949-54
title: Drummer Bruz Freeman and the Freeman family
summary: Sarah's drummer is the oldest of the musical Freeman brothers, completing a trio that lasted until Christmas 1953.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Anyway, Sarah got him to work with the group, and a drummer who really came from a musical family. I never did know what his first was -- we used to call him "Bruz" and his last name was Freeman. Bruz Freeman. Bruz had a brother that played guitar [GEORGE FREEMAN] and his other brother plays tenor saxophone [VON FREEMAN], and I think now one of his sons is quite a tenor player...

Von Freeman, Chico Freeman, George Freeman, they're all from the Freeman family. Well, Bruz I think is the oldest Freeman brother. He went out to California to live, after leaving Sarah, and I think I've seen him once or twice then. I don't even know whether he's playing drums at all now. But his brothers are very popular musicians these days, and very good ones, I understand.

But this formed Sarah Vaughan's first trio. I guess for about eight or nine months, we had maybe... .No, not eight or nine months. For almost a year, up until Christmas week of 1953, which I guess would probably be at least ten months that we worked together...
